title: How to Choose the Right Corrugated Box for Export Shipping
body:
# Choosing the Right Corrugated Box

Picking the correct corrugated box protects your goods and cuts freight costs.

## 1. Understand ply and flute
- **3-ply** suits light domestic parcels.
- **5-ply** is the workhorse for e-commerce and export.
- **7-ply** is for heavy or fragile machinery parts.

## 2. Match the bursting strength
Ask your supplier for the **Bursting Strength (BS)** and **Edge Crush Test (ECT)** values. For export, a BS of 16–20 kgf/cm2 is a safe baseline.

## 3. Size it to the product, not the shelf
Oversized boxes waste void-fill and volumetric weight. Share exact product dimensions so the box is built to fit.

## 4. Certifications that matter
Look for **ISO 9001** manufacturing and **FSC** certification if your buyer has sustainability requirements.

> Tip: order a small sample batch before committing to a large MOQ.

title: A Buyer's Guide to Sourcing Precision-Machined Auto Components
body:
# Sourcing Precision-Machined Auto Components

When you buy machined parts, the datasheet matters as much as the price.

## Confirm the tolerances
Ask for the drawing and the achievable tolerance band (e.g. **±10 microns**). A supplier who can't state this can't hold it.

## Ask about inspection
- Coordinate Measuring Machine (CMM) reports
- Magnetic-particle or dye-penetrant inspection for forged parts
- Material test certificates (MTC)

## Verify the quality system
For automotive, **IATF 16949** is the standard to insist on, alongside **ISO 14001** for environmental compliance.

## Plan for volume
Discuss MOQ, lead time, and whether the supplier can scale from prototype to series production without re-tooling delays.

title: PCB Sourcing 101: What Every Hardware Buyer Should Check
body:
# PCB Sourcing 101

A great design can still fail if the board is fabricated wrong. Here is what to verify before you place an order.

## Send clean Gerbers
Provide complete **Gerber + drill files**, a fab drawing, and a stackup note. Ambiguity leads to remakes.

## Specify the finish
- **HASL** is economical for through-hole.
- **ENIG** is flatter and better for fine-pitch and BGAs.

## Don't skip compliance
Insist on **RoHS** compliance and, where relevant, **UL** marking. Ask for the **ISO 9001** certificate of the fab.

## Quick-turn vs volume
Prototype houses optimise for speed; volume houses optimise for yield and cost. Choose the partner that matches your stage.

title: TMT Bars Explained: Fe-500 vs Fe-550 for Your Project
body:
# TMT Bars: Fe-500 vs Fe-550

Choosing the right grade of reinforcement steel balances strength, ductility and cost.

## What the grade means
The number is the **yield strength in N/mm2**. Fe-550 is stronger but less ductile than Fe-500.

## When to use which
- **Fe-500 / Fe-500D** — residential and general construction; better ductility for seismic zones.
- **Fe-550** — high-rise and heavily loaded structures where you want to reduce steel quantity.

## Always check certification
Buy only **BIS-certified** bars (IS 1786) and ask for the mill test certificate with each lot.

## Storage matters
Keep bars off the ground and covered to avoid rust that weakens the bond with concrete.
